Here's draft copy for both slides. One piece of math shapes it: $40k MRR is $480k ARR, and 10% month over month held for 12 months gets you to about $125k MRR ($1.5M ARR). Few companies hold 10% for two years, so the plan below assumes growth averages about 6.5% a month and reaches $1.5M ARR at month 18. Holding 10% is your upside case, not your plan.

Everything in [brackets] is a placeholder or an illustrative assumption. Replace it with your actuals before an investor sees it.

---

## Slide: Use of Funds

**Headline:** $3M takes us to Series A proof points in 18 months, with [24+] months of runway

| Area | Amount | % | Key additions | Milestone it serves |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Go-to-market | $1.20M | 40% | 2 AEs, 1 SDR/demand-gen hire, ~$[150]k of programs | Repeatable acquisition beyond founder-led sales |
| Product & engineering | $1.05M | 35% | 3 engineers | [Feature/integration] that unlocks larger contracts |
| Customer success | $0.30M | 10% | 1 CSM, onboarding tooling | Retention and expansion |
| G&A and infrastructure | $0.15M | 5% | Finance, legal, hosting growth | Clean books for Series A diligence |
| Reserve | $0.30M | 10% | Unallocated | Absorbs slippage in hiring or the Series A process |

**Footer:** Team grows from 6 to [13] by month 12. Amounts are shares of net burn by function, including today's team. Runway: [24+] months ($3M plus $[X] existing cash, at a planned average net burn of ~$[125]k/month). Instrument: [post-money SAFE / priced seed].

**Speaker note:** Hiring is gated on evidence, not the calendar. The second AE starts only after the first closes $[X] of new ARR in their first [90] days. If a gate slips, the money stays in the bank and runway gets longer.

## Slide: Milestones

**Headline:** What we will prove by month 18, when we raise our Series A

| Proof point | Today | Month 9 | Month 18 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ARR | $480k | ~$850k | $1.5M+ |
| Net revenue retention | [x]% | 100%+ | [110]%+ |
| Sales motion | Founder-led | First AE ramped | 2+ AEs at [70]%+ of quota |
| CAC payback | [x] months | Measured by channel | Under [18] months |
| Average contract value | $[x] | $[x] | $[2x], driven by [feature] |
| Customers | [N] | [N] | [N] |

**Closing line on the slide:** By month 18 we raise on a repeatable sales engine, not founder-led hustle.

**Speaker note:** The base case assumes growth averages ~6.5% a month. At today's 10%, we reach $1.5M ARR around month 12, which pulls the Series A forward. If growth drops below [5]%, we pause the go-to-market hires and stretch runway to [N] months.

---

## Before this goes in the deck

1. **Runway figure.** Send me cash on hand and your three-month average net burn. I'll compute the zero-cash date and the latest date you can start the Series A process with room for a slow round.
2. **Default-alive check.** At $40k MRR growing 10%, you may be close to default alive at today's burn. If you are, say so in the pitch. It strengthens your position in every negotiation.
3. **Metric definitions.** Footnote MRR on the slide (recurring subscription revenue only, excluding implementation and one-time fees) and use the same definition in the model and data room. Do the same for NRR and CAC payback.
4. **The Series A bars are heuristics.** The month-18 thresholds are common rules of thumb, not current market data. Bars move by year and sector, so check them against a dated source for B2B SaaS before you commit to them on a slide.
5. **Dilution.** $3M at a $[15]M post-money is 20% before any pool top-up. Put the round on the fully diluted cap table with any existing SAFEs and the pool increase before you set a cap or accept a valuation.
6. **Plan B.** If the round closes at $2M, decide now which hires drop and which milestone moves. Have that version of the slide ready before the first meeting.

Want me to turn the burn and hiring assumptions into a monthly model, so the runway number on the slide is computed rather than estimated?

**Before you send**

- **Keep the pilots from reading as revenue.** Don't write "signed two enterprise customers" or headline a pipeline figure. If a pilot is unpaid, say so.
- **Check confidentiality** in the pilot agreements before naming either company.
- **Use one revenue definition.** If the target was set on a different basis than the actual (bookings versus recognized revenue, say), state that in one line rather than letting the reader find it.
- **If the miss moves your zero-cash date, say so now.** If runway is now under about 12 months (a rule of thumb, not a standard), add plan B: cost cuts, an insider bridge, or other financing. Angels handle a miss far better than a surprise bridge request.
